instruments.name: Steel-string acoustic guitar
instruments.materials: a solid spruce soundboard, walnut back and sides, a mahogany neck and an ebony bridge
instruments.mechanism: six steel strings transfer vibration through the saddle and bridge into a braced wooden soundboard
instruments.heritage: European flat-top guitar making and North American steel-string accompaniment
instruments.innovation: the offset fan-X brace that keeps the bass side compliant while supporting the treble bridge wing
instruments.need: a quiet fingerstyle line that remains intelligible beneath a close vocal microphone
instruments.history: The 1962 AG-10 was a ladder-braced student guitar. A 1979 repair survey linked winter cracks to inconsistent spruce conditioning, prompting enclosed storage and individual moisture records. The 1996 AG-120 introduced a bolt-on neck to reduce the cost of resets. Northlight arrived in 2014 with the offset fan-X brace and a wider fingerstyle saddle. A 2022 bridge revision enlarged the glue footprint without increasing the visible bridge outline.
instruments.tradeoff: a lightly braced top responds quickly to a soft touch but needs tighter humidity control and less aggressive string tension
instruments.defect: a lifted bridge corner or a rising top behind the saddle
instruments.test: bridge-bond inspection followed by action measurement at the twelfth fret
instruments.limit: 2.2-2.6 mm bass-string action and 1.7-2.1 mm treble-string action, measured at the twelfth fret with the specified light-gauge strings
instruments.care: Keep the instrument at 40-55 percent relative humidity and loosen, rather than remove, all strings before long-term storage.

instruments.name: Solid-body electric guitar
instruments.materials: an alder body, a maple neck, a rosewood fingerboard and two passive humbucking pickups
instruments.mechanism: magnetic pickups convert steel-string motion into an electrical signal whose spectrum depends on pickup position and loading
instruments.heritage: mid-century amplified dance bands and later studio-oriented electric guitar design
instruments.innovation: a removable wiring rail that exposes the switch and jack without removing the strings
instruments.need: a repeatable clean-to-driven change without an audible level jump
instruments.history: The 1971 EG-20 used a single pickup and a painted ash body. Touring repairs in 1985 exposed a fragile jack socket, so the socket moved onto a replaceable plate. The 2003 EG-160 established two humbuckers and a fixed bridge. Switchrail launched in 2017 after dealer technicians tested a serviceable control assembly. A 2024 shielding change separated the pickup ground path from the removable control rail.
instruments.tradeoff: higher-output pickups drive an amplifier sooner but can obscure soft attacks and exaggerate noise in poorly shielded rigs
instruments.defect: an intermittent output jack or a scratchy control under rotation
instruments.test: continuity, shielding and output checks through a reference amplifier
instruments.limit: no intermittent signal during fifty jack insertion cycles and less than 1 dB level mismatch between the calibrated clean presets
instruments.care: Wipe strings after playing, keep the output jack free of cable strain and use only the specified truss-rod tool.

instruments.name: Four-string electric bass
instruments.materials: a chambered ash body, a laminated maple neck, a pau ferro fingerboard and a split-coil passive pickup
instruments.mechanism: four long steel strings excite a magnetic pickup while the neck and bridge determine the stability of the vibrating length
instruments.heritage: the transition from upright bass to portable amplified rhythm-section instruments
instruments.innovation: the twin-spine neck laminate that limits seasonal relief changes without adding an active preamplifier
instruments.need: a stable low E with enough midrange definition for a dense ensemble
instruments.second_use: pit-orchestra work with long seated sets
instruments.history: The 1974 EB-30 was built for dance-band rental fleets. A 1988 standing-player study led to a longer upper horn and better strap balance. In 2007 the EB-180 adopted the twin-spine neck laminate. Deepfield arrived in 2016 with controlled body chambers and a heavier bridge anchor. The 2023 service revision standardized the saddle screws across all three current models.
instruments.tradeoff: body chambering reduces shoulder load but removes material around hardware, so bridge anchorage needs explicit inspection
instruments.defect: a weak low-string attack caused by excessive pickup height or a loose bridge anchor
instruments.test: neck-relief, pickup-clearance and sustained low-note checks
instruments.limit: 0.25-0.40 mm neck relief at the seventh fret under the specified four-string set
instruments.care: Use the specified string gauge, check relief after seasonal changes and avoid lifting the instrument by its tuning machines.

instruments.name: Violin
instruments.materials: a carved spruce top, figured maple back and ribs, an ebony fingerboard and a fitted maple bridge
instruments.mechanism: a bowed string drives the bridge, with the bass bar and soundpost distributing motion through the carved body
instruments.heritage: the European four-string violin tradition and workshop-based plate graduation
instruments.innovation: the paired-flex plate record that matches top and back stiffness before assembly
instruments.need: a clear upper register that does not dominate the quartet at low dynamics
instruments.history: The 1959 VN-1 established the first Aster Vale production line. A 1976 return study found that standard soundpost lengths produced inconsistent response, so posts became individually fitted. The 1991 VN-90 introduced paired-flex records. Skylark launched in 2012 with a revised lower-bout arch. A 2021 fitting change improved access for reversible neck and fingerboard service.
instruments.tradeoff: a thinner top can feel lively under the bow but has less margin for aggressive soundpost pressure
instruments.defect: an open seam, a warped bridge or a soundpost fitted with excessive pressure
instruments.test: seam inspection and a controlled bow-response comparison across all four strings
instruments.limit: 195 mm body stop with a workshop tolerance of plus or minus 0.5 mm on the full-size models
instruments.care: Release bow tension after use, remove rosin dust with a dry cloth and ask a trained repairer to move the soundpost.
instruments.service: bridge replacement and reversible open-seam repair

instruments.name: Viola
instruments.materials: a broad spruce top, maple ribs and back, an ebony fingerboard and a compact neck heel
instruments.mechanism: four bowed strings tuned in fifths excite a body sized to balance a low C response with comfortable reach

instruments.need: a resonant C string on an instrument manageable during long rehearsals
instruments.history: The 1965 VA-12 was an enlarged violin pattern. Player feedback in 1982 prompted a shallower shoulder and a compact heel. In 2001 the VA-140 moved volume into the lower ribs rather than increasing body length. Hearth launched in 2015 with asymmetric rib depth. The 2024 neck template retained the same string length while easing the thumb transition into upper positions.
instruments.tradeoff: a larger internal air volume supports the low register but can make the instrument harder to hold if the shoulder geometry grows with it
instruments.defect: an uneven C-to-G transition or excessive reach caused by the wrong chinrest setup
instruments.test: low-register response and player-reach checks with the supplied fittings
instruments.limit: 405 mm body length and a 370 mm vibrating string length on all three standard models
instruments.care: Choose chinrest and shoulder support together, remove rosin dust daily and never force a tight tuning peg.
instruments.service: individual bridge fitting and peg adjustment

instruments.limit: a 690 mm vibrating string length and no endpin slip under a 180 N axial workshop load

instruments.name: Double bass

instruments.mechanism: four long strings tuned in fourths couple through the bridge to a large air cavity for bowed and plucked bass
instruments.heritage: orchestral bass practice and the portable rhythm-section bass of jazz ensembles
instruments.innovation: a replaceable neck-foot wedge that changes projection without invasive heel cutting

instruments.need: a clear plucked attack with enough sustain for a sparse trio
instruments.second_use: orchestral section playing with a bow
instruments.history: The 1970 DB-25 used a fully laminated body for rental durability. In 1993 the DB-100 adopted a carved top while retaining a robust laminated back. A 2008 repair programme introduced the replaceable neck-foot wedge. Dockside launched in 2018 with an adjustable bridge and clearer bowed-string spacing. The 2025 packing standard required a separate impact guard around the endpin housing.

instruments.defect: a loose neck-foot joint or bridge adjusters that no longer turn evenly
instruments.test: neck projection and bridge-adjuster load checks
instruments.limit: a 1050 mm vibrating string length and a matched adjuster height within 0.5 mm after setup
instruments.care: Support the body when moving it, retract the endpin and turn bridge adjusters only after reducing string tension.

instruments.name: Grand piano
instruments.materials: a laminated maple rim, spruce soundboard, cast-iron plate, high-carbon steel strings and felt-covered hammers
instruments.mechanism: a horizontal action throws hammers at strings and uses escapement and repetition levers to permit repeated notes
instruments.heritage: the development of the piano from early hammer keyboards to the modern concert grand
instruments.innovation: a numbered action cassette that preserves technician reference points when the action is removed
instruments.need: controlled repetition at low dynamics without an abrupt change in hammer tone
instruments.history: The 1981 GP-40 began as a compact salon grand. A 1997 technician programme standardized action-removal datums. The 2009 GP-180 introduced the numbered action cassette. Aurora launched in 2019 with a longer bass bridge and revised hammer felt. In 2024 the factory extended the settling interval between first stringing and final regulation instead of compressing it to meet shipping targets.
instruments.tradeoff: a heavier hammer can support a powerful attack but requires careful balancing to preserve soft control and fast repetition
instruments.defect: uneven repetition, a noisy damper return or an unstable bass unison
instruments.test: touchweight, repetition and unison stability checks after settling
instruments.limit: 48-54 g downweight in the middle register after final regulation; all 88 keys must pass the repetition sequence
instruments.care: Use a qualified piano technician, maintain a stable room climate and never apply polish to strings or the action.
stage_details: verify rim laminations before the form is released

instruments.materials: a spruce soundboard, laminated beech back posts, cast-iron plate and a vertical felt-hammer action

The 2006 UP-150 introduced a split service panel. Dayroom launched in 2018 with longer bass strings inside a taller cabinet. A 2025 pedal revision reduced linkage noise while retaining the mechanical practice mute.
instruments.tradeoff: a taller cabinet allows longer bass strings but requires more wall clearance and complicates transport through stairways
instruments.defect: a slow hammer return or a rattling practice-mute rail
instruments.test: return-speed and pedal-linkage checks at both soft and strong touch
instruments.limit: 50-56 g downweight in the middle register and no audible practice-rail rattle during the workshop repeated-note sequence
instruments.care: Leave room for rear ventilation, keep liquids off the top and schedule tuning after the instrument acclimates to its room.

instruments.second_use: chamber music with rapid enharmonic changes
instruments.history: The 1987 HP-50 was developed with a small orchestral repair team. In 2002 the workshop added a pedal-cycle test after discovering linkage noise only appeared after settling. The 2011 HP-190 introduced service-indexed disc carriers. Moonarc launched in 2020 with a reinforced soundboard shoulder. The 2025 transport revision added a dedicated neck-support cradle.
instruments.tradeoff: a strong soundboard must withstand high combined string load, but unnecessary mass reduces response in the middle register
instruments.defect: a noisy pedal linkage or a disc that does not engage the string cleanly
instruments.test: pedal-cycle, disc-engagement and string-clearance inspection
instruments.limit: all seven pedals must complete 200 workshop cycles without missed detents or metal-to-wood contact
instruments.care: Use the transport cradle, leave pedal regulation to a harp technician and replace strings with the specified material and gauge.

instruments.name: Concert flute
instruments.materials: a silver-alloy headjoint, silver-plated nickel-silver body, drawn tone holes and felt-backed pads
instruments.mechanism: an air jet splits at the embouchure edge and excites a cylindrical air column whose length changes with the keys
instruments.heritage: the transverse flute tradition and the nineteenth-century development of ring-key mechanisms
instruments.innovation: the removable crown spacer that provides a repeatable reference for headjoint service

instruments.history: The 1983 FL-60 used a plated headjoint and closed keys. A 1998 pad study moved final leak checks until after mechanism settling. The 2008 FL-170 introduced the removable crown spacer. Silverwake launched in 2016 with a revised embouchure cut. The 2024 footjoint revision standardized the service screws without changing the concert-C fingering system.
instruments.tradeoff: a freer embouchure cut can produce a broad tone but demands more control of air direction at soft dynamics

instruments.test: pad-leak and octave-response checks with a controlled air direction
instruments.limit: no visible leak under the workshop light test and linked-key closing lag below 20 ms on the bench fixture
instruments.care: Swab the bore after playing, keep the embouchure edge free of residue and never oil the pads.

instruments.heritage: the sackbut lineage and the orchestral tenor trombone with extended low-register access
instruments.innovation: the replaceable slide-crossbrace shim that lets a repairer correct alignment before replacing the complete outer slide
instruments.need: a smooth slide at fast tempo and an attachment that does not choke sustained low notes
instruments.history: The 1979 TB-28 had a straight tenor layout. A 1995 transport audit identified crossbrace impacts as the leading cause of slide drag. The 2008 TB-165 introduced a replaceable crossbrace shim. Broadreach launched in 2018 with an open-wrap F circuit. The 2024 release check began measuring slide movement after packing simulation, not only at the bench.
instruments.tradeoff: an open-wrap attachment reduces tight bends but occupies more space and needs stronger transport protection
instruments.defect: slide drag caused by misalignment or a dent on an inner-slide stocking
instruments.test: slide-straightness and lubricated travel checks before and after packing simulation
instruments.limit: the lubricated slide must traverse the bench fixture under the 1.2 N reference pull without local sticking
instruments.care: Clean and lubricate the slide as specified, keep the slide lock engaged during carrying and do not use the slide as a handle.
stage_details: inspect tube straightness before plating
match the inner-slide spacing to the outer assembly
record the fitted shim thickness
measure the gold-brass flare profile
check rotor timing and open-wrap clearance
repeat travel after the packing simulation

instruments.name: Pedal timpani
instruments.materials: a spun copper bowl, an aluminium frame, a synthetic membrane and a balanced pedal-linkage assembly
instruments.mechanism: a pedal changes membrane tension over a resonant bowl, shifting pitch while the head and bowl shape the decay
instruments.heritage: orchestral kettledrums and the later pedal systems that permit rapid pitch changes
instruments.innovation: the calibrated balance cartridge that separates pedal counterforce adjustment from head-tension adjustment
instruments.need: a pitch change that settles quickly without a pedal creeping back
instruments.history: The 1994 TP-90 used a hand-tensioned copper bowl. A 2007 orchestral trial established the balanced pedal frame. The 2015 TP-210 introduced a calibrated balance cartridge. Roundwave launched in 2021 with revised bowl-rim support. In 2025 the final test added a hold interval at both ends of the specified pitch range.
instruments.tradeoff: a light frame helps touring crews but must remain rigid enough to keep bowl support and pedal geometry consistent
instruments.defect: pedal creep or uneven membrane tension around the rim
instruments.test: head-clearing, pedal-hold and pitch-settling checks
instruments.limit: less than 5 cents pitch drift during a thirty-second hold at each end of the specified range after head settling
instruments.care: Cover the head when idle, release transport locks only after positioning and ask a percussion technician to change balance-cartridge settings.
stage_details: measure bowl depth and wall thickness
inspect bearing contact around the full rim
check linkage pivots without head load
equalize tension at every lug
match cartridge setting to the fitted membrane
record thirty-second holds after the settling sequence

instruments.name: Concert snare drum
instruments.materials: a six-ply maple shell, steel tension hoops, synthetic heads and a replaceable twenty-strand snare-wire set
instruments.mechanism: the struck batter head excites the shell and resonant head, which drives wires against the underside to create the snare response
instruments.heritage: military side drums and later orchestral instruments designed for very soft articulation
instruments.innovation: the indexed throw-off cradle that returns the wire tension to a recorded setting after disengagement
instruments.need: a quiet roll that speaks evenly without a wire rattle after the phrase
instruments.history: The 1990 SD-75 used a basic lever throw-off and a deep shell. A 2003 orchestral player trial favoured a shallower shell for soft articulation. The 2009 SD-170 introduced an indexed throw-off cradle. Threadmark launched in 2017 with revised snare beds. A 2024 service revision made the strap clamp replaceable independently of the throw-off body.
instruments.tradeoff: a sensitive wire setting reveals soft strokes but can produce sympathetic buzz when nearby instruments excite the resonant head
instruments.defect: an uneven snare bed or a throw-off that loses its tension setting
instruments.test: bearing-edge flatness and soft-roll response with repeated throw-off cycling
instruments.limit: wire tension must return within one index division after fifty engage-disengage cycles
instruments.care: Disengage the wires for transport, protect the resonant head and tighten opposing tension rods gradually rather than loading one side.
instruments.service: wire-set replacement and throw-off cradle adjustment
stage_details: check roundness before trimming
inspect the edge against a flat reference
measure bed depth on both sides
record the cradle index and strap position
alternate opposing rods to equalize load
repeat a soft roll after each throw-off cycle group
